Agent skills, and why this repo has them

10 procedures, one corpus, 4 runtimes. Written once, exported everywhere, each one tied to a command that fails when it is ignored.

The problem they solve

Every expensive mistake in this repo has the same shape: the obvious action was wrong for a reason the code does not state. cargo new produces a crate that compiles and shadows the inferred nx targets. cargo upgrade --incompatible bulldozes a pin that exists precisely to be skipped. A migration applied without re-hashing atlas.sum is green locally and breaks the operator in the cluster. Writing KCL next to the app is the intuitive layout and yields CannotFindModule.

A model — any model — reproduces those mistakes, because each one is the reasonable move. The fix is not a bigger prompt: rules only work if they arrive at the moment of the decision and carry the failure that motivated them.

So the repo splits its knowledge in two. AGENTS.md holds what is true on every single turn and is always in context. A skill holds a procedure that is long, conditional and only occasionally relevant: it stays on disk, announces itself with a one-line trigger, and is read in full only when a request matches. Nine of them, below.

What makes a skill legitimate

The same bar the platform-tool registry uses, for the same reason: a documented rule nobody can check rots into a claim. Every row in docs/agents/registry.toml must state the failure it prevents, cite files a reader can open, and name the command that goes red if the skill is ignored. A skill with no gate is not deleted — it is declared as a gap, with an owner and a closing condition, and it is shown as ungated here.

One corpus, four runtimes

The procedure is authored once, as .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Every other runtime gets a generated adapter, so a fix to a procedure cannot reach one vendor and miss another.

RuntimeHow it gets the skillArtifact
Claude CodeNative skill, auto-loaded when the description matches the request.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Gemini CLI/skill:<name> custom command; @{…} injects the same SKILL.md verbatim.gemini/commands/skill/<name>.toml
AWS BedrockHosted agent: instruction + the SKILL.md as a knowledge-base documentdist/agents/bedrock/ (build output)
GCP Vertex AI (ADK)Hosted ADK agent: instruction + the SKILL.md in a RAG corpusdist/agents/vertex/ (build output)

Hosted agents have no checkout, so they get two pieces: a short instruction that routes and forbids (capped at Bedrock's 4000-character instruction limit, which the generator enforces), plus the full SKILL.md as a retrieval document. Producing those files is free and local — task agents-export; creating the hosted agents costs money and stays a human decision.

The skills

cncf-manager

adopted scope:infra

Prose is not proof. README.md listed Istio + Kiali as prerequisites for months while the repo contained no control plane, no CR and no canary — an agent reading that prose would have "kept" a mesh that never existed, or installed one to make the docs true. This skill makes adoption a claim the repo can reproduce (install path + consumer + gate) and makes anything paid stop for a human signature, which is the one decision an agent must never take alone.

Fires when
Evidence-driven evaluation, adoption, drift-audit and retirement of infrastructure/CNCF-landscape tooling (mesh, gateway, gitops, operators, scanners, SaaS). Human approval is REQUIRED before anything paid. Use when asked "do we actually use X?", when adding/replacing/removing a platform tool or operator, when a tool appears in docs but maybe not in the cluster, or when a change introduces a paid plan, seat, quota or SaaS token.
Proven by
task tooling-check
Evidence
docs/tooling/registry.toml · docs/tooling/service-mesh.md · tools/tooling/check-registry.ts

db-migration

adopted scope:tasks

One schema change is four artifacts that must agree: the timestamped .up.sql, schema.sql, atlas.sum and the migrations ConfigMap. Only the first is obvious from the request, and the failure mode of skipping the re-hash is invisible locally — a stale atlas.sum breaks the Atlas Operator at apply time, in the cluster, long after the PR went green.

Fires when
Add or modify a database schema migration (Atlas versioned mode). Use when changing table schemas, adding columns/indexes, or when the user mentions migrations, schema.sql, or AtlasMigration.
Proven by
task migrate-validate DB=<db>
Evidence
scripts/tasks/db.yml · manifests/db/terran/migrations · manifests/db/terran/schema.sql

Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

deps-maintenance

adopted scope:infra

cargo upgrade --incompatible is the obvious command and the wrong one: it bulldozes deliberate range pins — testcontainers = "=0.27.3" is exact-pinned precisely so it is skipped — and it runs no OSV scan, no npm cooldown and no post-check. Every update therefore goes through upkg, and a failed run prints a diagnosis block that is only actionable if you know how to read it.

Fires when
Update dependencies or diagnose a failed upkg run. Use when the user asks to update/upgrade deps, runs task upkg/weekly, or pastes output containing BEGIN-UPKG-DIAGNOSIS or OSV-Scanner failures.
Proven by
task check (post-upkg) + task scan
Evidence
scripts/tasks/flows.yml · apps/todo/web-leptos/osv-scanner.toml · Cargo.toml
Runtimes
Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

kcl-package

adopted scope:infra

Manifests are rendered by a PINNED KCL package that lives in a SIBLING repo and is consumed as an OCI artifact. The intuitive move — write the .k files next to the app — was tried (apps/terran/*/k8s) and produced CannotFindModule. Publishing and bumping the package is a cross-repo procedure with a registry, a tag and a consumer pin, none of which is discoverable from this repo alone.

Fires when
Create, version and publish a KCL package as an OCI artifact to a registry of the user's choice (Docker Hub, ghcr.io, a local kind registry), and consume it from this repo. Use when adding or bumping a KCL package, changing [k8s] package/tag in butler.toml, or when kcl mod push/kcl run oci:// fails.
Proven by
task k8s-check
Evidence
butler.toml · docs/tilt-generators.md
Runtimes
Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

lefthook-format

adopted scope:infra

The obvious hook — run the whole-tree formatter and stage_fixed the result — commits only the staged files but rewrites every other file in the working tree, reformatting someone's unrelated WIP. The per-file forms each have a trap the task leaves never hit: bare rustfmt formats as edition 2015, explicit paths make typos --write-changes ignore _typos.toml excludes and rewrite vendored htmx, and just's {{files}} splits a path with a space. Exported to local runtimes only: git hooks run in a checkout.

Fires when
Wire formatters into git hooks with lefthook — staged-file fixers on pre-commit, read-only gates on pre-push — calling the formatter binary directly, through task, through just, or any shell command. Use when editing lefthook.yml, adding/changing a formatter in a hook, when a hook rewrites files you did not stage, or when hooks do not run at all.
Proven by
task hooks-check
Evidence
lefthook.yml · scripts/tasks/flows.yml · _typos.toml · biome.json
Runtimes
Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

new-rust-crate

adopted scope:shared

cargo new is wrong here in four ways at once: dependency versions live only in the root [workspace.dependencies], members is an explicit alphabetical list and not a glob, the layer a crate lands in decides what it may depend on, and a hand-written project.json silently SHADOWS the nx targets the local plugin infers — 27 such files were deleted for that reason. A crate scaffolded by instinct compiles and still breaks the graph.

Fires when
Scaffold a new Rust crate (lib or app) in this workspace. Use when adding a domain lib, core lib, contract crate, or a new service/API binary.
Proven by
task lint-rust
Evidence
Cargo.toml · tools/nx/plugin.ts · tools/nx/scope-tags.ts · scripts/tasks/rust.yml

Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

precommit-review

adopted scope:shared

The model that wrote the code knows the intent and therefore forgives itself. The fix is two passes with different blind spots over ONE frozen input: the staged index, not anyone's memory of the edit. The bundle is also the only thing that stops a secret-shaped path reaching a vendor CLI — coderabbit and codex transmit the WORKING TREE, not the index.

Fires when
Two-pass review of a staged change before it is committed — pass 1 by the model that wrote the code, pass 2 by independent components (reviewer + security-reviewer subagents, CodeRabbit CLI, Codex CLI) that never see pass 1. Use before any commit of non-trivial code, when asked to review changes / "review before commit" / run /precommit, or when a change is about to go into a PR.
Proven by
task review-bundle
Evidence
tools/review/bundle.ts · .claude/commands/precommit.md
Runtimes
Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

repo-maintenance

adopted scope:infra

Scheduled maintenance is the one flow with no human in the loop, across three repos, with a token that can push. Everything in the playbook is a rail: PRs only, never main, never force-push, one branch per task, no gate no PR, and pre-existing failures get reported rather than "fixed" by loosening the gate. It is exported to Claude Code only because the rails themselves are Claude Code hooks — see the hook-enforced-only gap.

Fires when
Scheduled/hub maintenance playbook for nx-playground, kcl-packages and dotconfig — drift gates, pin freshness, dependency refresh via upkg, issue/PR triage — delivered as pull requests only. Use when running .github/workflows/claude-maintenance.yml, when asked to "do maintenance" on one of the three repos, or when triaging stale issues/PRs.
Proven by
no gate — declared gap hook-enforced-only: The invariants that matter (never commit on main, never force-push, no secret material in a diff) are enforced at tool-call time by .claude/hooks/guard-git.js and .claude/hooks/guard-secrets.js, which are Claude Code hooks. No task can assert them, and no other runtime has an equivalent — a Gemini/Bedrock/Vertex agent running this playbook is on the honour system. Closes when the guards are re-implemented as a pre-commit/pre-push hook in git itself, so every runtime inherits them.
Evidence
.github/workflows/claude-maintenance.yml · .claude/hooks/guard-git.js · .claude/hooks/guard-secrets.js
Runtimes
Claude CodeGemini CLIAWS BedrockGCP Vertex AI (ADK)

rust-architecture-audit

adopted scope:shared

Every shortcut in a layered workspace is locally reasonable: one SQL query in a handler, one if status == in a service, one domain crate depending on its neighbour. Each is invisible in review and permanent in effect. The audit turns placement into findings tied to a command that fails when the finding is ignored, so "where should this logic go" has a checkable answer instead of a preference.

Fires when
Audit where Rust logic lives and how it is managed across this workspace's crate layers (apps → domains → core/contracts) — layer placement, anemic models, logic leaking into apps or handlers, cross-domain coupling, service-boundary hygiene, duplication. Use when asked to review/check/audit the architecture, "where should this logic go", "is this in the right crate/layer", before extracting a service, or when a PR adds business rules, SQL, or a domain dependency to an app.
Proven by
task boundaries
Evidence
docs/modular-monolith-architecture.md · docs/adr-tasks-service-boundary.md · tools/nx/check-boundaries.ts

service-transport

adopted scope:shared

"How should A talk to B" is answered by the repo, not by taste: one broker (NATS JetStream), one proto module, one HTTP toolkit, Postgres NOTIFY for browser realtime — Kafka and RabbitMQ are already status = "rejected". Without this, an agent adds a second broker or a second gRPC binary over tables an existing service already serves on one port, and the cost is a permanent transport to maintain.

Fires when
Choose and wire a communication surface between processes — NATS JetStream topics/event architecture, gRPC, or plain HTTP/REST (plus Postgres NOTIFY for browser realtime). Use when adding a stream/subject/consumer/worker, a proto service or gRPC client, a REST endpoint or outbound HTTP call, or when asked how service A should talk to service B.
Proven by
task proto-lint
